why: This is a historically specific Iowa certification-examination requirement prescribing which psychology textbooks candidates must study, rather than a reusable instructional element or named product.

The closest page is [principle] Adaptive Learning (58), but it lacks the distinct recommendation that an adaptive system make its learner model inspectable and negotiable through interaction with the learner.

The candidate and open candidate A share the general principle that adaptive educational systems should give learners meaningful control over how adaptation operates, here through inspection and negotiation of the learner model.

Interactive open learner modelling is a narrower adaptive-learning practice in which learner diagnosis and subsequent support are negotiated with the learner rather than inferred and used solely by the system.

rejected.verifier: The claim concerns improving the learner model, not evidence that adapting tasks, hints, checks, or sequencing improves aligned learning.
The claim concerns reflective thinking through open learner modelling, not performance-responsive task, hint, or pacing adaptation.

why: The Iowa Assessments are a named, validated achievement-test product administered by schools, not a general instructional element or research method.
name: Iowa Assessments
product_description: The Iowa Assessments are nationally normed, school-administered achievement tests measuring student performance in reading, mathematics, science, and related academic domains, developed and distributed by Riverside Insights.

why: The recommendation to use a competence-oriented performance examination that empirically observes and evaluates performance rather than only outcomes is a narrower case of Competency-Based Assessment.
